programme.desc: A reformed man tries to make an honest living for himself and his family after his jail term. His life takes an ugly turn when a woman claims him to be her husband and he is also framed for murder.

programme.desc: A brash and honest policeman is torn apart between his duties and saving his family when his own brother is caught in a blue-film scam. He also must protect a sole witness whose life is in danger.

programme.title: Jagan

programme.title: Barah Aana
programme.desc: Three men accidentally stumble into the world of crime when they start kidnapping for small ransoms in order to improve their lifestyles. However, they soon realise that it is not a bad business.

programme.title: Aar Ya Paar
programme.desc: Shekhar is having an affair with Anu, his wealthy wife's secretary. When the wife finds out, they kill her. The police then find evidence against him, and he learns that Anu is likely to betray him.

programme.title: Jaane Jigar
programme.desc: Two women look identical but hail from different backgrounds. They fall in love with Ravi and Vijay who are best friends. Misunderstandings arise when they believe they are in love with the same girl.

programme.title: Race

programme.title: Papi Gudia

programme.title: Storage Wars
programme.desc: S14 E1 — The Hunchy-Back of La HabraThe buyers try their luck at a new facility in La Habra, where Ivy decides to teach them a lesson. Dusty brews himself up an interesting unit, while Kenny weighs the value of childhood memories when selecting a locker.

programme.title: Storage Wars
programme.desc: S14 E2 — The 300th Times the Charm!Ivy dons his bright white lucky sneakers in Van Nuys. Brandi and Lisa's friendship is tested as they go head to head on a pair of lockers. Kenny sets his fears aside and takes the plunge on a unit that might just immerse him in profit.

programme.title: Storage Wars
programme.desc: S14 E3 — You Can Lead a Horse to a LockerBarry and Kenny show up in their alternative fuel vehicle, Lisa does her best to break the curse of the bad locker, while Ivy finds some curious denominations.

programme.title: Storage Wars
programme.desc: S14 E4 — Piles to Go Before I KeepLaura takes the reigns alone in Fullerton and proceeds to outsell Dan. Brandi gets assaulted by her locker but ultimately drives home a winner. Rene postpones a day date in favour of a work date, while Darrell stumbles across and unexpected collection.

programme.title: Storage Wars
programme.desc: S14 E5 — In Pain in the MembraneIn Victorville, a friendly duel runs Dusty up, though his mother lode of vinyl might just save him. Ivy's locker shines some light on the business, while Lisa learns that she needs her locker about as much as she needs a hole in her head.

programme.title: Storage Wars
programme.desc: S14 E6 — How the West Covina Was WonIn West Covina, Lisa is so busy looking back that she makes the worst auction mistake. Rene finds a bargain and really makes the most of it. Ivy unfolds his way to a profit and unloads some stuff onto Lisa.

programme.title: Storage Wars
programme.desc: S14 E7 — King of Orange ChickenRene shows up in Orange, declaring himself the King, while Dusty isn't quite ready to concede the title. Kenny accidentally re-invents the wheel, while Lisa sees things from a slightly different perspective.

programme.title: Storage Wars
programme.desc: S14 E8 — Lego My LockerThe units are packed full in Stanton, as Darrell has to deal with Kimber's eyes on a competitor. Ivy brings a full truck, hoping for a second haul. Dusty unpacks what could be the ultimate assistant, while Rene's hunch serves him well.

programme.title: Deal or No Deal
programme.desc: Airing from 2005 to 2009 on NBC, the game show series returns to primetime TV with original host Howie Mandel. A contestant must choose from 26 sealed briefcases containing a marker for various amounts of cash -- from one penny to $1 million. The player then eliminates the remaining 25 cases one by one. The chosen ones are opened and the amount of money inside revealed. After several cases are opened, the player is tempted by the Banker to accept an offer of cash in exchange for not continuing the game and possibly winning a larger sum of money.

A contestant must choose from 26 sealed briefcases containing a marker for various amounts of cash -- from one penny to $1 million. The player then eliminates the remaining 25 cases one by one. The chosen ones are opened and the amount of money inside revealed. After several cases are opened, the player is tempted by the Banker to accept an offer of cash in exchange for not continuing the game and possibly winning a larger sum of money.

Family comedy sequel, starring Zachary Gordon and Steve Zahn.

programme.title: Mary Berry Everyday
programme.desc: S1 E1 — Delicious MemoriesMary travels to Scotland to enjoy the best of their everyday larder with recipes inspired by her own Scots heritage. She discovers wonderful shellfish in Ullapool, and shares the joy of venison cooked on a BBQ with chef Tom Kitchin.

programme.title: Mary Berry Everyday
programme.desc: S1 E2 — Hearty and WholesomeMary shares inspiring everyday dishes full of wholesome goodness from her secret tip for a rich bolognese to a heartwarming soup. She dons a white suit and tries her hand at beekeeping, collecting fresh honey to make a winning pud.

programme.title: The Pioneer Woman
programme.desc: S15 E7 — Kit for Cowboy CameronRee Drummond welcomes a new cowboy to the ranch with a frontier-style dinner kit of his favourite food, including short rib sandwiches, roasted butternut squash salad and salted caramel frosted brownies.

programme.title: The Pioneer Woman
programme.desc: S15 E8 — Old-Fashioned ComfortIt's comfort from start to finish and Ree's spelling it out in an old-fashioned, feel-good way. She cooks up tuna noodle casserole, meatballs in sweet and sour sauce, glazed apple dumplings and Welsh rarebit.

programme.title: Jamie's 15 Minute Meals
programme.desc: S1 E15 — Rosemary Chicken and Happy Cow BurgersOn the menu are rosemary chicken, grilled polenta and porcini tomato sauce, plus burgers, old-school coleslaw and corn on the cob.

programme.title: Jamie's 15 Minute Meals
programme.desc: S1 E16 — Sticky Squid Balls and Sausage FusilliJamie cooks sticky squid balls, grilled prawns and noodle broth, plus sausage fusilli and creamy garden salad.

programme.title: Be My Guest With Ina Garten
programme.desc: S3 E3 — Laura LinneyIna Garten welcomes stage and screen actor Laura Linney to her home with a fruity blueberry ricotta breakfast cake; in honour of Laura's Southern heritage, Ina teaches her how to make shrimp boil with a twist.

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off
programme.desc: S12 E4 — Dessert WeekIt's Dessert Week, and the bakers put their twist on the classic pavlova, take on a toffee technical, and create a delicate dessert wrapped in intricately patterned sponge for the showstopper.

programme.title: Rachel Allen: Bake!
programme.desc: S1 E4 — Quiche Lorraine/Pink MeringuesRachel bakes a quiche Lorraine, meets German "Konditormeister" Falko Burkert, and learns how to make a cake on a spit known as a Baumkuchen, or tree-cake.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E6 — LancashireJames continues his British adventure in Lancashire with top local chef Lisa Allen in the passenger seat of his trusty red mini. Their first stop is an incredible food hall in Lisa's home town of Clitheroe. Here they shop and then cook together a fantastic BBQ'd John Dory with kohlrabi and fennel salad. Next, Lisa is in the driving seat as she takes the mini to a local buffalo farm where they're producing some interesting cheese from buffalo milk.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E7 — SnowdoniaJames' adventure brings him over the border into North Wales, where he's joined by chef Stephen Terry for this leg of his journey. Their first stop is the grand Pale Hall, where head chef Gareth Stevenson is cooking up a real treat - Moroccan-inspired Welsh lamb. James offers his own variation of Welsh lamb in the grounds of the hall, serving with gnocchi and vegetables. Next, one of James' boyhood dreams comes true as he has the ultimate falconry experience.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E13 — NorfolkJames Martin's British adventure travels as far to the east of England as this journey will go, to Norfolk, where he is joined by his good old mate and top local chef, Galton Blackiston. They meet in Cromer, where Galton has a successful fish and chip shop, which inspires James to cook pan-fried cod with a warm tartar sauce on the beach. Then James heads to Norfolk Lavender to find out why it grows so well in this county and how it's distilled for oil.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E14 — London and BrayNo adventure around the UK would be complete without a trip to the capital city, London. James is checking out some of his old haunts and stopping in on Clare Smyth's brand-new restaurant Core for a bite to eat and a catch-up with the world's best female chef. Then high up on the rooftops of London, he cooks up spiced pigeon breast with dhal. Next, James ventures into south-east London to a knife forgery in Peckham. He gets hands on in the process of making Japanese style knives.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: S8 E8 — Comfort Food ClassicsGuy travels the country for homemade comfort food.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: S8 E9 — Twists and TraditionsGuy Fieri visits America's most interesting and unique restaurants. Guy finds a farm restaurant in New York, a fishing shop turned eatery in California, and a Mexican joint with tuna tacos in Ohio.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: S8 E10 — Fresh and FunkyGuy Fieri visits America's most interesting and unique restaurants. Guy finds fresh crab in San Francisco, homemade granola in Nevada, and boiled turkey in North Carolina.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: S8 E11 — Triple D Goes HawaiianGuy Fieri visits America's most interesting and unique restaurants. In Hawaii Guy goes to a waterside spot with a real catch of the day, a hot dog place with lobster dogs and a luau with roasted pig.

programme.title: Man v Food
programme.desc: S1 E11 — PortlandIn Portland, Oregon, Adam takes on the 'Great Balls of Fire' challenge of five habanero chilli cheese fritters drenched in habanero hot sauce.

programme.title: Man v Food
programme.desc: S1 E12 — SeattleAdam Richman's journey brings him to Seattle, Washington, and Red Mill Burgers, which serves onion rings that are voted the best in the country. Then it's on to The Crab Pot for a huge plate of seafood.

programme.title: Cake Boss
programme.desc: S14 E1 — Fiery Dragons And Marrying CatsBuddy turns up the heat with a fire-breathing dragon cake for a modern-day medieval knight. Plus, a cat café wants Mary to make a cake for a feline wedding - and to officiate it!

programme.title: Cake Boss
programme.desc: S14 E2 — Wedding Bells And Flower PowerBuddy meets a floral-loving bride who wants bouquets of flower cupcakes for her big day. Plus, Mauro celebrates his 25th wedding anniversary with Madeline in romantic style!

programme.desc: S1 E5 — Tarte Tatin/Chocolate CakeToday's treats include Tarte Tatin, with caramelised apples. In Callander, baker Tom Lewis reveals the secrets of his delicious bread.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E8 — PembrokeshireJames and Stephen head south through Wales en route to Pembrokeshire. But before they get there, they stop to visit Gareth Ward and his stunning restaurant Ynyshir. After filling their bellies, they make it to the coast where James cooks up his Marloes Sands seafood parcel. Stephen tracks down Wales' answer to Willy Wonka, young chocolatier Liam Burgess, who helps him make a very special one-off chocolate bar for James.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E9 — Northern Irish CoastJames' British adventure has crossed over the Irish Sea to Northern Ireland, where he is joined by his great pal and famous local chef, Paul Rankin. Paul goes in search of Irish gold and finds it in the form of rapeseed at the Kane family farm in Limavady.

programme.title: Myra Hindley: The Untold Story
programme.desc: The stories of the victims and those who got away.

programme.title: Mafia's Greatest Hits
programme.desc: Ex-FBI agent Joe Pistone, who infiltrated the Mafia for six years as mobster `Donnie Brasco', reveals how his undercover work led to over 100 convictions.

programme.title: Mafia's Greatest Hits
programme.desc: Financier Allen Dorfman used union pension funds to bankroll the Mafia and the FBI quickly realised they could bankrupt the Mob by pursuing Dorfman.

programme.title: Mafia's Greatest Hits
programme.desc: Joe Valachi was the first Mafia member to break the Mob's code of silence and turn public informer, revealing the term `Cosa Nostra' to the world.

programme.title: Heartland Homicide
programme.desc: When hardware store clerk Sydney Loofe vanishes after an online date, investigators race against the clock to find her. But as the days wear on, a horrible truth emerges from the darkness.

programme.title: When Fred Met Rose
programme.desc: Documentary series examining what led Fred and Rose West to become serial killers.

programme.title: Fred and Rose: The West Murders
programme.desc: Focuses on the notorious house which the couple shared in Gloucester. But when they moved into 25 Cromwell Street, the couple began to kill for sexual thrills.

programme.title: Fred and Rose: The West Murders
programme.desc: Looks at how a dogged police officer, Hazel Savage, fought to have the Wests' patio excavated when she became suspicious about the whereabouts of their daughter. The film also includes insights from both Fred and Rose West's former solicitors.

programme.title: Mafia's Greatest Hits
programme.desc: Gambino family soldier Roy DeMeo and his crew were suspected of killing dozens of people and dismembering their bodies, but the FBI and other mobsters were soon on his trail.

programme.title: Mafia's Greatest Hits
programme.desc: Meyer Lansky was an associate of `Lucky' Luciano and linked to criminal financial operations, but the FBI struggled to pin anything on him - or find his riches.

programme.title: Mafia's Greatest Hits
programme.desc: The final episode of this gripping series reveals what happened when the FBI pursued the five clans who ran organised crime in New York, as well as the fate of two brave informers.

programme.title: Trevor McDonald and the Killer Nurse

programme.title: Wayne Couzens: Killer in Plain Sight
programme.desc: This extraordinary film reveals the shocking truth about the serving police officer who killed Sarah Everard, and asks how he was able to hide from scrutiny for so long.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E6We trace the astonishing story of designers turning away from metal and back to wood to create a twin-engine bomber that could outrun almost any aircraft in the sky, yet deliver a bomb load greater than an Avro Lancaster.

programme.title: The Lost Women Spies
programme.desc: E1During WWII, the French Resistance seeks aid from SOE. Led by Vera Atkins, Odette Sansom and Noor Inayat Khan fight the Nazis, risking it all for victory.

programme.title: The Lost Women Spies
programme.desc: E2Vera enlists Violette Szabo and Yvonne Baseden. With circuits failing and Noor at risk, treachery allegations harm preparations for the Allied invasion.

programme.title: Combat Machines
programme.desc: E1Examining moments of engineering ingenuity which made the difference between triumph and disaster on the battlefield - beginning with World War I.

programme.title: Combat Machines
programme.desc: E2Examining the machines used by iconic military unit 'The Desert Rats' in the North African desert campaign of World War II.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E5John F Kennedy first made news in 1943 when, as a skipper of a torpedo boat in the Pacific, he and his crew were shipwrecked. We tell the story of their rescue.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E6We explore two submarines – former Cold War enemies now moored in a Kent river, and discover the story of Vasili Arkhipov, a Soviet submariner who refused to authorise a nuclear launch.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E1The Grumman Avenger, which was the most important carrier-based torpedo bomber on American and British carriers throughout the Second World War. They were also the biggest and heaviest carrier aircraft of the conflict.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E2The Junkers Ju 52, which is considered one of the most famous airplanes in history. It was first designed as an airliner, but was used as a transport, bomber, and air ambulance during the Second World War.

programme.title: The Lost Women Spies
programme.desc: E3With Allied victories and the liberation of Paris following D-Day, Vera is in a race against time to locate her missing agents.

programme.title: The Lost Women Spies
programme.desc: E4Armed with evidence from Odette, Vera intensifies her search at Karlsruhe prison and Ravensbruck, facing hurdles to uncover crucial results in Germany.

programme.title: Hell On Earth: WWII
programme.desc: E3The United Kingdom is isolated as German forces occupy Europe. 17,000 Trains carry German armies towards the Soviet Union. With Operation Barbarossa Hitler launches Vernichtungskrieg, a war of annihilation.

programme.title: Hell On Earth: WWII
programme.desc: E4After Pearl Harbour and their triumphant sweep across South-East Asia, Japanese armies celebrate their victory. But Japanese confidence is shaken four months later at the Battle of the Coral Sea.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E3The definitive, if not the best, Axis fighter of World War two: we delve into the story of legendary ace Adolf Galland and examine in detail and example of the type in his colours. We also look at the technical heritage the 109 designers left.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E4The story of the prolonged development and the initially troubled operational history of the Boeing B-29 Superfortress. Forever known as the airframe that dropped the first atomic weapons on Japan, the B-29 lived on well beyond its war years.

programme.desc: E4The story of the prolonged development and the initially troubled operational history of the Boeing B-29 Superfortress. Forever known as the airframe that dropped the first atomic weapons on Japan, the B-29 lived on well beyond its war years.

programme.title: Combat Machines
programme.desc: E1Examining moments of engineering ingenuity which made the difference between triumph and disaster on the battlefield - beginning with World War I.

programme.title: Soviet Storm
programme.desc: E10In August 1945 the Red Army launched a devastating assault against Japanese-occupied Manchuria on the same day Japan suffered its second nuclear attack, which helped force the Japanese leadership to recognise that the war was lost.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E3A chronological telling of the dramatic D-Day story, focusing on vessels that made the landings possible. From the X-Craft lying on the seabed days before the invasion to battleships like USS Texas and HMS Belfast that bombarded the Normandy beaches.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E4We pinpoint the moment the USA became a global superpower when we recreate how the USS Olympia won the Battle of Manila Bay, and we show how the revolutionary British HMS Dreadnought brought ship design into the 20th century.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E1The F15 Eagle immediately turned the tide of the first Gulf War to prove its greatness. Our immaculately restored MiG Killer was involved in one of the most bizarre combat incidents during that conflict, and has survived to tell the tale.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E2The mighty Flying Fortress takes to the air as we examine the background and development of one of WWIIs most iconic bombers. Serving with both the USAAF and the RAF, we see it in action and fly a surfing example.

programme.title: Dictators' Hideouts
programme.desc: E3Paranoid and isolated, Albanian dictator Enver Hoxha establishes his bunkerization project, which would result in the construction of more than 170,000 bunkers, including the top secret HQ in Tirana, and a bunker city known as The Capital of War.

programme.title: Dictators' Hideouts
programme.desc: E6A secret bunker below the Kremlin, a sanctuary in the coastal forests of Sochi and a hidden second Metro in Russia’s capital are just some of the bunkers developed for Stalin, seen for the first time ever using recently declassified documentation.

programme.title: Combat Machines
programme.desc: E3Examining the machines used by iconic military unit 'The Desert Rats' in the North African desert campaign of World War II.

programme.title: Combat Machines
programme.desc: E4We examine the robot that defused bombs both on foreign battlefields and British streets, and an astonishing Gulf War minelayer.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E7We tell the story of two rescues that ended in tragedy – the sinking of the hospital ship Britannic, and the Lancastria, rescuing soldiers and civilians from France in 1940. In the 19th century, USS Constellation chased down slave ships.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E8Ships don't have to be large to change the course of history. The Smithsonian has a small 1776 wooden gunboat, built to stop a British invasion and two Japanese midget submarines were part of the attack on Pearl Harbour.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E3The Republic P-47 Thunderbolt, a Second World War fighter aircraft produced by the American company Republic Aviation from 1941 until 1945. It was considered a successful high-altitude fighter and also served as the foremost US fighter-bomber in the ground-attack role.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E4The Yakovlev Yak-3, a Second World War Soviet fighter that was regarded for its performance at low altitudes and its agility. It was one of the most successful Soviet aircraft designs of the war.

programme.title: Greatest Escapes of WWII
programme.desc: E1Colditz Castle, the foreboding Nazi fortress that became a university of escapology; The Great Escape, and the doomed airmen of Stalag Luft Three; and the most daring breakout of them all, the ‘Warburg Wire Job’.

programme.title: Greatest Escapes of WWII
programme.desc: E2An adrenaline-fuelled dash through nazi-occupied Europe known as ‘The Flight of the Crow’, a death-defying escape across the world’s most perilous mountain range, and the largest escape of world war two - by men who chose death over dishonour.

programme.title: Nazi Murder Mysteries
programme.desc: E3A true story in which we see how the Berlin murder squad came up against the Nazi regime's ideologies, hindering the investigation and letting a serial killer slip through their fingers.

programme.title: Nazi Murder Mysteries
programme.desc: E4A macabre discovery was made on the Hagely Estate in the West Midlands, UK. Hidden in a Wych Elm tree was the skull of a woman. When the police investigated further they found a full skeleton, bits of clothing and the remains of the woman's hand.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E5The Heinkel He 111 is one of the most recognised German aircraft of WW2. The broad winged design was a guinea pig for future bombers, with more variants than any other military aircraft of the time.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E6We trace the astonishing story of designers turning away from metal and back to wood to create a twin-engine bomber that could outrun almost any aircraft in the sky, yet deliver a bomb load greater than an Avro Lancaster.

programme.title: Dictators' Hideouts

programme.title: Nazi Murder Mysteries
programme.desc: E1As the Nazis waged a war of destruction across Europe, women travelling on Berlin’s S-Bahn train network were being stalked in the carriages at night. During the wartime blackouts, a serial killer used the darkness to carry out a reign of terror.

programme.title: Nazi Murder Mysteries
programme.desc: E2In 1943, the mysterious murder of one of the wealthiest men in the British empire, Sir Harry Oakes, sparked a chain of events that have led many to believe that the Duke of Windsor had not learned from his mistakes.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E5The Heinkel He 111 is one of the most recognised German aircraft of WW2. The broad winged design was a guinea pig for future bombers, with more variants than any other military aircraft of the time.

programme.title: Combat Machines

programme.title: Cracking The Code
programme.desc: E3The Japanese Super Code reveals the US efforts to crack Japan's unbreakable WWII code following the horror of the attack on Pearl Harbor.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E5John F Kennedy first made news in 1943 when, as a skipper of a torpedo boat in the Pacific, he and his crew were shipwrecked. We tell the story of their rescue.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E6We explore two submarines – former Cold War enemies now moored in a Kent river, and discover the story of Vasili Arkhipov, a Soviet submariner who refused to authorise a nuclear launch.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E3Often called 'the forgotten bomber', the mighty North American twin delivered the first blow in the fight back against Japan, in one of the most daring and audacious raids of all time.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E4Cruelly called 'the packing case the B17 came in,' the Liberator more than proved its worth over Europe and the Pacific, patterning the B17 to deliver a blow to the axis powers in WWII however it wasn't simply a bomb delivery system.

programme.title: Al Murray: Why Do The Brits Win Every War
programme.desc: E1Frenchman Fred Sirieix joins Al Murray to break down what really happened during the Napoleonic wars. Did Britain really win the battle of Waterloo?

programme.title: Al Murray: Why Do The Brits Win Every War
programme.desc: E2Al joins forces with German comedian Henning Wehn to delve deeper into the truth behind some World War II myths.

programme.title: Combat Machines
programme.desc: E5Exploring the machines that hide in the shadows, capturing, transmitting and analysing vital combat information.

programme.title: Combat Machines
programme.desc: E6In 1961, Soviet T-54 tanks and American M-48 Patton tanks face off at Checkpoint Charlie in Berlin.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E9Learn about life on a Tudor ship from objects found on the Mary Rose, while on HMS Victory discover the battle-winning tactics of Admiral Nelson.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E10In 1939, the German raider Atlantis was equipped with fake funnels and her sailors dressed as women pushing prams to fool Allied merchant ships. We also look at how merchant ships were painted with bizarre shapes to fool U-boats.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E5The Hawker Hurricane was the first RAF aircraft to fly over 300mph. Over half of every enemy aeroplane destroyed in the Battle of Britain was by a Hurricane, not a Spitfire.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E6The McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II. Regarded as one of the most important aircraft of the Cold War. It was a major part of the United States Air Force, Navy and Marine Corps, and was also used by many other countries.

programme.title: Al Murray: Why Do The Brits Win Every War
programme.desc: E3Bruno Tonioli joins Al to look at key battle tactics during the Roman Invasion back in AD 43.

programme.title: Al Murray: Why Do The Brits Win Every War
programme.desc: E4Al faces up to the richest nation on Earth to discover how the former British colony of America somehow slipped through its fingers.

programme.title: The Abyss: Rise And Fall Of The Nazis
programme.desc: E5In 1934, Hitler's government is firmly in the saddle. Most Germans support Hitler's anti-Jewish policy and the regime's terror soon escalates.

programme.title: The Abyss: Rise And Fall Of The Nazis

programme.title: The Abyss: Rise And Fall Of The Nazis
programme.desc: E4President Hindenburg suspends freedom of speech and Hitler comes to power in 1933. The first concentration camps for political opponents are set up.

programme.desc: E5The aircraft capable of delivering the payload of a B17, in a single post war air frame. The many variants of this single piston engined fighter bomber helped dominate the air to ground attack role in Vietnam, earning quite a reputation.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E6The definitive combat helicopter saw first blood in South East Asia and has been transport, gunship, smoke ship, command centre, MediVac and dozens of other roles. We hear and see it's hair raising missions and watch it earn its fame.

programme.title: Commando Missions
programme.desc: E1In the north of Crete, six commandos land in a cove. On this island that has been occupied for two years, they have been given a high-risk mission—to infiltrate the Heraklion airfield to destroy the Luftwaffe bombers and fighter planes.

programme.title: Commando Missions
programme.desc: E2December 7th, 1942. Off the coast of France, ten British commandos board five canoes in the middle of the ocean. Their objective: to paddle to the Gironde estuary, then up the river to Bordeaux to sabotage German ships.

programme.title: Combat Machines
programme.desc: E7A look at the military engineering used as US and South Vietnamese forces attempt to overcome North Vietnam and the Viet Cong.

programme.title: Combat Machines
programme.desc: E8A look at the origins of the Arms Race between the USA and the Soviet Union, and the nuclear weapons that ended WWII.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E1Viking combat ships changed the course of history. Their longships brought William the Conqueror’s troops to Hastings, adventurers to North America and raiders to plunder the Saxon kingdoms.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E2In Stealth we examine the methods ships have used to evade detection. With the advent of radar in WW2, ships that wanted to remain undetected had to find ways to hide.
